meta.title: CoinW Agent Skill · MVP Roadmap
meta.description: Turn an Agent into the trading brain of every CoinW user — from reading the market to placing orders in one sentence. Nine steps from v1.0 to v2.0, all on the table.

hero.title: Let the Agent trade for you. From signal to fill, one sentence away.
hero.subtitle: This is not a slide deck. Every version number ships a mini demo you can click, run, and watch the next step unfold. v1.0 gets it running, v2.0 closes the loop, and the nine steps in between cover the whole thing — tech path, safety, merge-back plan.

act1.title: Runs
act1.desc: Version one doesn't need to be smart. It needs to work end to end. Read the market, place an order, check a position — the Agent treats the exchange like an API.

act2.title: Contained
act2.desc: Put the Agent in a sandbox. Multi-wallet, risk controls, alerts, a low-friction entry — it can't run wild, and it can't lose the user's money.

act3.title: Grows
act3.desc: The Agent picks its own Skills, writes its own strategies, grades its own results. v1.5 is the Agent Zone. v2.0 merges back into the main site. The end state: a trading brain that evolves.

v10.headline: The exchange becomes the Agent's raw material
v10.lede: This is the one the boss can click today. Five user stories, 18 Must capabilities, 9 Phase-1 extras, and a one-click install command. This is all of Agent Skill phase one, on one page. Built to the PRD. No theatrics.

v11.headline: One sentence, end to end
v11.lede: A chat box on the left, a Skills panel on the right. You type, the Agent calls Skills, the result streams back. No real LLM — it's a dialog tree mock. All three v1.0 stories walk through.

v12.headline: One user, several wallets
v12.lede: Even retail users run spot plus futures plus staking. The Agent has to know which one you mean. Permission tiers go from two-level to four: read, spot, futures, full. Anything out of scope gets refused on the spot.
bullets: Wallet-aware · the Agent reads your fund layout
Four-tier permissions · least privilege, not all-or-nothing
Out-of-scope block · wrong wallet, wrong call — platform says no
User-visible trace · every call logs which tier it went through

v13.headline: Teach the Agent to ask once
v13.lede: The scary part of Agent trading isn't making the wrong call. It's making the wrong call silently. Large-trade confirmation is the brake: above the threshold you set, the Agent has to stop and ask. Simple, effective, lifesaving when it matters.
bullets: Configurable threshold · by dollar or by position %
Timeout policy · if you don't answer, default (reject or hold)
Full audit trail · every confirmation chain logged

v14.headline: Can't run an Agent? Just type in TG.
v14.lede: Not everyone has their own Agent. Not everyone can configure MCP. v1.4 drops the entry barrier to zero — a TG bot command or email subscription gets the same Skills. First net for incremental users.
bullets: TG bot · one line equals a full Agent call
Email subscription · digest / alerts / portfolio to inbox
Same source · identical Skills, matching results
Zero setup · no install, no config, sign up and go

v15.headline: Agents pick their own Skills and build their own plays
v15.lede: In the first four versions, the Agent is used by people. From v1.5 it flips — the Agent browses the Skill Marketplace, builds its own strategies, runs its own backtests. A central Agent node, Skills orbiting, animated connections. The first shape of "grows".

security.headline: Four diagrams, zero hand-waving
security.lede: Before a new module ships, four questions always come up inside the company: what does the architecture look like, how does it most likely get attacked, how does the dev pipeline prevent leaks, and how does it merge back to the main site without blowing up. These four diagrams answer all of it.

v20.headline: A trading brain that evolves
v20.lede: v2.0 is not another version. It's the closing point for the nine before it. The Agent can see, think, place orders, stay contained, find Skills, grade itself, and merge back. The day the full chain runs end to end, Agent Skill graduates from "a feature module" into "a category".
